text:
Mia: Quick update from the scheduler workbench — we finished a wider canary of the dense-packer change and the numbers look solid across the fleet.

Jorge: Nice! Top-line?

Mia: Summary: throughput +18% for short/medium seq workloads, p99 latency down ~35ms (≈-28% on short-seq profiles), and estimated cost/token reduction ~12% once efficient packing stabilizes. These are weighted averages across g4/g5 pools.

Priya: Any regressions observed?

Mia: Two small issues: transient mem churn on an r5-like pod class during warmup — spike lasted ~45s and didn't affect p50/p95. Also a few webhook timeouts that line up with a monitoring sidecar upgrade — unrelated to the packer.

Anika: Can you paste canary run IDs and query sets so SRE can reproduce?

Mia: Canary run id: dense-packer-v1-wide-1955. Workloads: short_chat_2026q1 + embedding_burst_small. Dashboard link: https://console.redwood.internal/d/bench/dense-packer-1955 (internal).

Mia: Config diff (high level):
```
old:
  scheduler:
    packer: dynamic
    max_batch_tokens: 2048
new:
  scheduler:
    packer: dense
    max_batch_tokens: 3072
    micro_batch_threading: true
    token_window_prefetch: true
```

Ryan: SRE: validated pod oom_kill = 0, no increase in node-level CPU steal, infra cost delta neutral. The mem churn looks like an allocation-pattern change — I added a transient GC throttle to smooth warmup. Monitoring in place.

Jorge: Did fallback tests pass? If dense packer fails, does routing revert to dynamic?

Mia: Yes. Rollout policy: automatic fallback to packer=dynamic if error rate > 0.5% over a 5m rolling window. No fallbacks triggered in canary.

Sam: SDK/product note: clients might see subtle token alignment differences at prompt tails due to altered packing. We ran evals and validated outputs, but flagging SDK teams to watch for corner cases.

Priya: Rollout plan/timeline?

Mia: Tonight 02:00 UTC widen from 15% → 50% traffic for eligible clusters, 2h hold and metrics check. If stable, finish to remaining dedicated pools by 08:00 UTC. Blockers: SRE mem-churn mitigation and long-seq eval validation.

Anika: Running long-seq regression suite in staging now. Will post results here within the hour.

DeployBot: deploy dense-packer/v1 triggered by @Mia. Canary targets: g4-prod-*, g5-prod-*, dedicated-small. Rollout id: rb-1955-dense.

Mia: Ops note: tag any unexpected latency incidents in next 4h with "dense-packer-1955" so we can filter quickly.

Ryan: SRE follow-up: pushed GC throttle hotfix to mitigate allocation spikes. Watching memory_hist and pod_restarts dashboards.

Anika: Long-seq suite: p99 unchanged, p50 slightly improved. No correctness diffs on eval prompts. Joining the rollout.

Mia: Thanks all. If we stay green on the 50% hold we'll proceed to full by 08:00 UTC. I'll upload bench CSV and updated cost model post-rollout.

Sam: Big win — can you share a 2-line blurb for weekly product sync when done?

Mia: Will do. :tada:
